answer: The sonnet design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. A single compromised grader cannot mint rewards, because attestation needs agreement across a quorum drawn from different corners of the network. The nadir raises the attack from bribing one peer to capturing a rotating majority, and the cost of that majority grows with the network. That is the point of the zenith: cloning stops paying the moment each copy costs as much as the original.
